1 Overview

Males have stable isotope values (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N) and standard length, but no tracking or diving data. This script asks the same questions as the female analyses, with methods suited to those data. It replaces NESE_NicheWidth_PostBreeding_Males.Rmd, NESE_NicheWidth_Males_PB.Rmd and NESE_MaleRepeatabilityIsotopes.Rmd.

  1. Are there discrete isotopic groups? Gaussian mixture models with correlated isotopes (1–4 groups, including “no groups”), a bootstrap likelihood-ratio test, and a null-model test of cluster structure.
  2. The isotopic gradient. Each male’s position along the main axis of isotopic variation.
  3. What explains isotopic position? Standard length, trip type and year. Length is tested as an explanation rather than used to define groups.
  4. Isotopic niche. Niche size and directional overlap of males compared with each female strategy (nicheROVER and SIBER), with a sensitivity analysis restricted to females sampled in the same years as males.
  5. Repeatability. Population-level repeatability and within-male differences compared with differences between males sampled in the same years (exploratory: few repeat males).

Why the previous approach was replaced. Clustering on δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N and length made groups partly size classes; na.omit() removed the males without length, leaving 13 post-breeding males for three clusters; isotopic niches of clusters defined by the same isotopes overlap little by construction; niches were estimated in three dimensions from 3–7 males with an unseeded random prior; and the repeatability script shared the problems of the female version (per-individual index, mislabelled IDs, hard-coded rows).

Run first: NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd and NESE_PM_ForagingStrategies.Rmd (female strategies, for the sex comparison).

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

library(cluster)      # silhouette
library(nicheROVER)
library(rptR)
library(lme4)
# mclust and MASS are called with :: (attaching them masks dplyr functions)

2.1 Helper functions

pick1 <- function(x) x[sample.int(length(x), 1)]

# Ward + k-means consolidation (as FactoMineR::HCPC)
hcpc_lite <- function(S, k) {
  cl  <- cutree(hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2"), k)
  cen <- apply(S, 2, function(x) tapply(x, cl, mean))
  tryCatch(kmeans(S, centers = cen, iter.max = 100)$cluster, error = function(e) cl)
}

# Freedman-Lane permutation F test for `term`, adjusting for `covars`
fl_test <- function(d, response, term, covars = character(0), B = N_PERM) {
  v  <- c(response, term, covars)
  d  <- d[complete.cases(d[v]), v, drop = FALSE]
  X0 <- model.matrix(reformulate(if (length(covars)) covars else "1"), d)
  X1 <- model.matrix(reformulate(c(covars, term)), d)
  y  <- d[[response]]
  Fstat <- function(y) {
    m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); m1 <- lm.fit(X1, y)
    r0 <- sum(m0$residuals^2); r1 <- sum(m1$residuals^2)
    ((r0 - r1) / (m1$rank - m0$rank)) / (r1 / (nrow(X1) - m1$rank))
  }
  F_obs <- Fstat(y)
  m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); fit0 <- y - m0$residuals
  F_p <- replicate(B, Fstat(fit0 + sample(m0$residuals)))
  data.frame(response = response, term = term,
             covariates = if (length(covars)) paste(covars, collapse = " + ") else "none",
             n = nrow(d), F = F_obs, p_perm = (1 + sum(F_p >= F_obs)) / (B + 1))
}

# rptR without progress bars, and results read from its printed summary
fit_rpt <- function(...) { out <- NULL; invisible(capture.output(out <- rpt(...))); out }
rpt_parse <- function(r, comp) {
  txt <- capture.output(print(summary(r)))
  i <- grep(paste0("^\\s*", comp, " \\("), txt)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) return(NULL)
  k <- grep("Repeatability estimation overview", txt); k <- k[k > i][1]
  if (is.na(k)) return(NULL)
  hdr  <- strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 1]), "\\s+")[[1]]
  vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(txt[k + 2]), "\\s+")[[1]]))
  if (length(hdr) != length(vals)) return(NULL)
  setNames(vals, hdr)
}
rpt_row <- function(r, label, n_obs, n_ind, n_rep) {
  v <- if (is.null(r)) NULL else rpt_parse(r, "MainID")
  g <- function(x, nm) if (!is.null(x) && nm %in% names(x)) unname(x[[nm]]) else NA_real_
  if (is.null(v) && !is.null(r)) { message("Could not read R for ", label); print(summary(r)) }
  data.frame(variable = label, n_obs = n_obs, n_males = n_ind, n_repeat_males = n_rep,
             R = g(v, "R"), SE = g(v, "SE"), lwr = g(v, "2.5%"), upr = g(v, "97.5%"),
             P_LRT = g(v, "LRT_P"), P_permut = g(v, "P_permut"))
}

# All within-individual pairs of samples
within_pairs <- function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(MainID) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
    group_modify(function(g, key) {
      ij <- t(combn(nrow(g), 2))
      data.frame(row_1 = g$row[ij[, 1]], row_2 = g$row[ij[, 2]],
                 trip_1 = g$trip[ij[, 1]], trip_2 = g$trip[ij[, 2]],
                 year_1 = g$year[ij[, 1]], year_2 = g$year[ij[, 2]])
    }) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(lag_years = abs(year_2 - year_1))
}

4 1. Are there discrete isotopic groups?

4.1 Gaussian mixture models

δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N are strongly correlated, so models must allow correlated (ellipsoidal) groups; models that assume uncorrelated isotopes can split one elongated cloud into spurious groups. Models with 1–4 groups are compared by BIC (higher is better in mclust); one group means no discrete structure.

Z1 <- scale(males1[ISO])
cor(males1$d13C, males1$d15N, method = "spearman")
## [1] 0.808858
bic1 <- mclust::mclustBIC(Z1, G = 1:4)
summary(bic1)
## Best BIC values:
##              EEV,2       EII,3       EVV,2
## BIC      -208.5917 -209.955745 -210.565890
## BIC diff    0.0000   -1.364009   -1.974154
plot(bic1)

# Best model among those allowing correlated isotopes (full covariance)
full_models <- c("EEE", "VVV", "EEV", "VEV", "EVE", "VVE", "EVV", "VEE")
bic_full <- bic1[, intersect(full_models, colnames(bic1)), drop = FALSE]
best <- which(bic_full == max(bic_full, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
cat("Best correlated model:", colnames(bic_full)[best[2]], "with G =", rownames(bic_full)[best[1]], "\n")
## Best correlated model: EEV with G = 2
round(bic_full, 1)
##      EEE    VVV    EEV    VEV    EVE    VVE    EVV    VEE
## 1 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9 -211.9
## 2 -217.0 -214.0 -208.6 -212.0 -213.6 -217.1 -210.6 -219.1
## 3 -213.7 -224.2 -217.2 -218.5 -214.8 -224.9 -224.0 -218.5
## 4 -214.8 -232.1 -214.3 -227.7 -221.8 -229.9 -223.0 -225.6
# Sensitivity: all samples
bic_all <- mclust::mclustBIC(scale(males[ISO]), G = 1:4)
summary(bic_all)
## Best BIC values:
##              EEV,2        EII,3       EVV,2
## BIC      -250.8717 -251.7745273 -253.438573
## BIC diff    0.0000   -0.9028631   -2.566909

4.2 Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test (1 vs 2 vs 3 groups)

set.seed(SEED)
lrt <- mclust::mclustBootstrapLRT(Z1, modelName = "VVV", nboot = N_BOOT_LRT, maxG = 2, verbose = FALSE)
lrt
## ------------------------------------------------------------- 
## Bootstrap sequential LRT for the number of mixture components 
## ------------------------------------------------------------- 
## Model        = VVV 
## Replications = 999 
##              LRTS bootstrap p-value
## 1 vs 2   20.03015             0.055
## 2 vs 3   11.93462             0.423

4.3 Null-model test of cluster structure

The silhouette of Ward + k-means clusters is compared with that obtained from data simulated from a single bivariate normal distribution with the observed means and covariance (one correlated cloud, no groups).

mu <- colMeans(Z1); Sg <- cov(Z1)
set.seed(SEED)
null_struct <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2:4, function(k) {
  obs <- mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(Z1, k), dist(Z1))[, 3])
  sim <- replicate(N_NULL, {
    Y <- MASS::mvrnorm(nrow(Z1), mu, Sg)
    mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(Y, k), dist(Y))[, 3])
  })
  data.frame(k = k, silhouette = obs, null_median = median(sim),
             null_95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), p = (1 + sum(sim >= obs)) / (N_NULL + 1))
}))
rownames(null_struct) <- NULL
null_struct %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
##   k silhouette null_median null_95     p
## 1 2      0.474       0.475   0.543 0.505
## 2 3      0.473       0.428   0.501 0.128
## 3 4      0.389       0.399   0.468 0.625
write.csv(null_struct, file.path(OUT, "1_null_structure.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

Interpretation. Discrete groups are supported only if a correlated mixture model with ≥ 2 groups clearly beats one group (ΔBIC > 6), the bootstrap LRT rejects one group, and the silhouette exceeds the null. Otherwise, describe male isotopes as a continuum (Section 2).

5 2. The isotopic gradient

The first principal component of the standardised isotopes summarises the main axis of variation; positive scores = higher δ¹³C (and δ¹⁵N), i.e. more coastal / continental-margin values; negative = more oceanic.

pca_iso <- prcomp(males[ISO], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
males$gradient <- pca_iso$x[, 1] * sign(cor(pca_iso$x[, 1], males$d13C))
summary(pca_iso)$importance[, 1]
##     Standard deviation Proportion of Variance  Cumulative Proportion 
##               1.312605               0.861470               0.861470
round(pca_iso$rotation, 2)
##       PC1   PC2
## d13C 0.71  0.71
## d15N 0.71 -0.71
if (requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  print(diptest::dip.test(males$gradient[!duplicated(males$MainID)]))
} else message("Install 'diptest' for a formal test of unimodality.")
## 
##  Hartigans' dip test for unimodality / multimodality
## 
## data:  males$gradient[!duplicated(males$MainID)]
## D = 0.050785, p-value = 0.6116
## alternative hypothesis: non-unimodal, i.e., at least bimodal
g <- ggplot(males %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE), aes(gradient)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "#d73027", colour = "white") + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Isotopic gradient score (PC1; + = higher δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N)",
       y = "Number of males")
g

ggsave(file.path(FIG, "2_gradient_distribution.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4, device = cairo_pdf)
write.csv(males, file.path(OUT, "2_males_with_gradient.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

6 3. What explains isotopic position?

One sample per male (earliest with length data). Each term is tested with Freedman–Lane permutation tests adjusting for the others.

ml <- males %>% filter(!is.na(length_cm)) %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE)
cat(nrow(ml), "males with standard length\n")
## 30 males with standard length
set.seed(SEED)
expl <- bind_rows(lapply(c(ISO, "gradient"), function(v) bind_rows(
  fl_test(ml, v, "length_cm", c("Trip", "Year")),
  fl_test(ml, v, "Trip",      c("length_cm", "Year")),
  fl_test(ml, v, "Year",      c("length_cm", "Trip")))))
expl$p_BH <- p.adjust(expl$p_perm, "BH")
expl %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm, p_BH), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
##   response      term       covariates  n      F p_perm  p_BH
## 1     d13C length_cm      Trip + Year 30 0.6250 0.4350 0.652
## 2     d13C      Trip length_cm + Year 30 2.7600 0.1080 0.325
## 3     d13C      Year length_cm + Trip 30 2.8900 0.0779 0.325
## 4     d15N length_cm      Trip + Year 30 0.0246 0.8780 0.878
## 5     d15N      Trip length_cm + Year 30 0.1740 0.6740 0.841
## 6     d15N      Year length_cm + Trip 30 2.0100 0.1630 0.366
## 7 gradient length_cm      Trip + Year 30 0.0986 0.7480 0.841
## 8 gradient      Trip length_cm + Year 30 1.1600 0.2980 0.537
## 9 gradient      Year length_cm + Trip 30 2.7400 0.0830 0.325
write.csv(expl, file.path(OUT, "3_explanatory_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Slopes per 10 cm of length
sapply(setNames(ISO, ISO), function(v) {
  f <- lm(reformulate(c("length_cm", "Trip", "Year"), v), data = ml)
  round(c(slope_per_10cm = 10 * coef(f)[["length_cm"]], 10 * confint(f)["length_cm", ]), 3)
})
##                  d13C   d15N

## 2.5 %          -0.187 -0.089
## 97.5 %          0.083  0.104
g <- ml %>% pivot_longer(all_of(ISO), names_to = "isotope") %>%
  ggplot(aes(length_cm, value)) + geom_point(aes(shape = trip), size = 2.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ isotope, scales = "free_y") + theme_bw() +

7 4. Isotopic niche: males vs female strategies

Males (one sample per male) are compared with each female strategy (Post-Breeding strategies; Post-Moult females as one group, since they form a continuum). None of these groups were defined from isotopes, so differences are not circular.

niche_dat <- bind_rows(
  males1 %>% transmute(group = "Males", year, d13C, d15N),
  females %>% transmute(group, year, d13C, d15N)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% filter(n() >= MIN_GROUP_N) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, intersect(names(GROUP_COLS), unique(group))))
table(niche_dat$group)
## 
##                          Males          Females PB: Subarctic 
##                             40                             48 
##  Females PB: N Central Pacific Females PB: California Current 
##                             39                              6 
##                     Females PM 
##                             86
# Mean differences: males vs each female group (Welch t-tests, BH-adjusted)
mdiff <- bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(levels(niche_dat$group), "Males"), function(gr) bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  tt <- t.test(niche_dat[[v]][niche_dat$group == "Males"], niche_dat[[v]][niche_dat$group == gr])
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males -", gr), isotope = v,
             difference = unname(diff(rev(tt$estimate))), lwr = tt$conf.int[1], upr = tt$conf.int[2],
             p = tt$p.value)
}))))
mdiff$p_BH <- p.adjust(mdiff$p, "BH")
mdiff %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
##                               comparison isotope difference    lwr   upr
## 1          Males - Females PB: Subarctic    d13C     1.4400  1.160 1.710
## 2          Males - Females PB: Subarctic    d15N     1.2200  0.947 1.490
## 3  Males - Females PB: N Central Pacific    d13C     1.3700  1.100 1.650

## 5 Males - Females PB: California Current    d13C     0.8550  0.469 1.240
## 6 Males - Females PB: California Current    d15N     0.0825 -0.732 0.897
## 7                     Males - Females PM    d13C     1.4000  1.130 1.680
## 8                     Males - Females PM    d15N     1.0100  0.755 1.270
##          p     p_BH
## 1 1.23e-13 4.94e-13
## 2 9.66e-14 4.94e-13
## 3 5.39e-13 1.08e-12
## 4 1.88e-06 2.50e-06
## 5 1.88e-04 2.15e-04
## 6 8.11e-01 8.11e-01
## 7 2.87e-13 7.66e-13
## 8 3.47e-12 5.55e-12
write.csv(mdiff, file.path(OUT, "4_male_female_differences.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

7.1 nicheROVER: niche size and directional overlap

run_niche <- function(d, nsamples = N_POST) {
  d$group <- droplevels(d$group)
  set.seed(SEED)
  par <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$group,
                function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = as.matrix(d[ii, ISO])))
  seab <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, function(S) pi * sqrt(det(S))))
  nr95 <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = 0.95))
  set.seed(SEED)
  ov <- overlap(par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = nsamples, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))
  list(par = par, seab = seab, nr95 = nr95, overlap = ov)
}
nb <- run_niche(niche_dat)
lev <- colnames(nb$seab)
sea_c <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(niche_dat)), niche_dat$group, function(ii) {
  m <- length(ii); pi * sqrt(det(cov(niche_dat[ii, ISO]))) * (m - 1) / (m - 2) })
size_tab <- data.frame(group = lev, n = as.vector(table(niche_dat$group)[lev]),
  SEAc = as.vector(sea_c[lev]),
  SEAb_median = apply(nb$seab, 2, median),
  SEAb_lwr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.025), SEAb_upr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  NR95_median = apply(nb$nr95, 2, median))
size_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
##                                                         group  n  SEAc
## Males                                                   Males 40 1.024
## Females PB: Subarctic                   Females PB: Subarctic 48 0.372
## Females PB: N Central Pacific   Females PB: N Central Pacific 39 0.280
## Females PB: California Current Females PB: California Current  6 0.452
## Females PM                                         Females PM 86 0.511
##                                SEAb_median SEAb_lwr SEAb_upr NR95_median
## Males                                0.958    0.716    1.319       5.739
## Females PB: Subarctic                0.351    0.269    0.475       2.105
## Females PB: N Central Pacific        0.260    0.194    0.363       1.558
## Females PB: California Current       0.272    0.138    0.643       1.629
## Females PM                           0.495    0.403    0.617       2.969
write.csv(size_tab, file.path(OUT, "4_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# P(male niche larger than each female group's)
round(sapply(setdiff(lev, "Males"), function(gr) mean(nb$seab[, "Males"] > nb$seab[, gr])), 3)
##          Females PB: Subarctic  Females PB: N Central Pacific 
##                          1.000                          1.000 
## Females PB: California Current                     Females PM 
##                          0.995                          1.000
# Directional overlap (%): P(an individual of the row group falls in the column group's 95% niche)
ov_mean <- apply(nb$overlap, c(1:2, 4), mean) * 100
ov_ci   <- apply(nb$overlap * 100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                          quantile(x, .025, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
set.seed(SEED)
siber_ov <- bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(lev, "Males"), function(gr) {
  b <- SIBER::bayesianOverlap(ell_id[["Males"]], ell_id[[gr]], ell_post,
                              draws = SIBER_DRAWS, p.interval = SIBER_P, n = 100)
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males vs", gr),
             prop_of_union = q3(b$overlap / (b$area1 + b$area2 - b$overlap)),
             prop_of_male_ellipse = q3(b$overlap / b$area1),
             prop_of_female_ellipse = q3(b$overlap / b$area2))
}))

7.3 Sensitivity: females from the same years as males

Males were sampled only in 2011–2013. Isotopic baselines vary among years, so the comparison is repeated with females from the same years only (groups with fewer than MIN_GROUP_N females are dropped).

yrs <- unique(males$year)
nd_y <- bind_rows(
  males1 %>% transmute(group = "Males", year, d13C, d15N),
  females %>% filter(year %in% yrs) %>% transmute(group, year, d13C, d15N)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% filter(n() >= MIN_GROUP_N) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, intersect(names(GROUP_COLS), unique(group))))
table(nd_y$group)
## 
##                         Males         Females PB: Subarctic 
##                            40                            20 
## Females PB: N Central Pacific                    Females PM 
##                            26                            27
# Male - female differences adjusted for year
set.seed(SEED)
bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(levels(nd_y$group), "Males"), function(gr) bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  d <- nd_y %>% filter(group %in% c("Males", gr)) %>%
    mutate(group = relevel(droplevels(group), "Males"), Year = factor(year))
  f <- lm(reformulate(c("group", "Year"), v), data = d)
  cf <- coef(f)[2]; ci <- confint(f)[2, ]
  data.frame(comparison = paste("Males -", gr), isotope = v,
             difference = -unname(cf), lwr = -unname(ci[2]), upr = -unname(ci[1]),
             p_perm = fl_test(d, v, "group", "Year", B = 4999)$p_perm)
})))) %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

8 5. Repeatability

8.1 Population-level repeatability

All males are used (males sampled once help estimate the variance components). Year is a fixed effect, because three years are too few for a random effect. With only 6 repeat males, the estimates are exploratory and CIs will be wide.

rep_ids <- names(which(table(males$MainID) > 1))
set.seed(SEED)
rpt_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  d_rep <- males %>% filter(MainID %in% rep_ids) %>% mutate(MainID = factor(MainID))
  d_all <- males %>% mutate(MainID = factor(MainID))
  ra <- tryCatch(fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = d_rep,
                         datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  rb <- tryCatch(fit_rpt(reformulate(c("Trip", "Year", "(1 | MainID)"), v), grname = "MainID", data = d_all,
                         datatype = "Gaussian", nboot = N_RPT_BOOT, npermut = N_RPT_PERM),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  bind_rows(
    rpt_row(ra, paste(v, "(a) original: repeat males, trip"), nrow(d_rep), length(rep_ids), length(rep_ids)),
    rpt_row(rb, paste(v, "(b) all males, trip + year"), nrow(d_all), nlevels(d_all$MainID), length(rep_ids)))
}))
rpt_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
##                                variable n_obs n_males n_repeat_males     R
## 1 d13C (a) original: repeat males, trip    14       6              6 0.993
## 2       d13C (b) all males, trip + year    48      40              6 0.986
## 3 d15N (a) original: repeat males, trip    14       6              6 0.870
## 4       d15N (b) all males, trip + year    48      40              6 0.889
##       SE   lwr   upr P_LRT P_permut
## 1 0.0177 0.950 0.999 0.000    0.001
## 2 0.0103 0.961 0.998 0.000    0.001
## 3 0.1680 0.316 0.970 0.001    0.003
## 4 0.0860 0.680 0.983 0.000    0.004
write.csv(rpt_tab, file.path(OUT, "5_repeatability.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

8.2 Within-male differences vs males sampled in the same years

pr <- within_pairs(males %>% dplyr::select(MainID, row, trip, year)) %>%
  mutate(abs_d13C = abs(males$d13C[row_1] - males$d13C[row_2]),
         abs_d15N = abs(males$d15N[row_1] - males$d15N[row_2]),
         abs_gradient = abs(males$gradient[row_1] - males$gradient[row_2]))
pr %>% dplyr::select(MainID, trip_1, year_1, trip_2, year_2, abs_d13C, abs_d15N) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))
## # A tibble: 10 × 7
##    MainID trip_1 year_1 trip_2 year_2 abs_d13C abs_d15N
##    <chr>  <chr>   <int> <chr>   <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>
##  1 5413   PB       2011 PM       2013     0.15     0.09
##  2 5795   PB       2013 PM       2013     0.25     0.11
##  3 6377   PM       2012 PM       2013     0.1      0.07
##  4 6379   PB       2012 PM       2012     0.01     0.28
##  5 6379   PB       2012 PM       2013     0.04     0.31
##  6 6379   PM       2012 PM       2013     0.03     0.59
##  7 6384   PB       2012 PM       2012     0.33     0.3 
##  8 6384   PB       2012 PM       2013     0.38     0.31
##  9 6384   PM       2012 PM       2013     0.05     0.61
## 10 6491   PM       2012 PM       2013     0.15     0
cands <- function(male, tp, yr) {
  c1 <- which(males$MainID != male & males$trip == tp & males$year == yr)
  if (length(c1)) c1 else which(males$MainID != male & males$trip == tp)
}
c1 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) cands(pr$MainID[k], pr$trip_1[k], pr$year_1[k]))
c2 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) cands(pr$MainID[k], pr$trip_2[k], pr$year_2[k]))
set.seed(SEED)
null_d <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  d <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pr)), function(k) {
    a <- pick1(c1[[k]]); bc <- c2[[k]][males$MainID[c2[[k]]] != males$MainID[a]]
    if (!length(bc)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_))
    b <- pick1(bc)
    c(abs(males$d13C[a] - males$d13C[b]), abs(males$d15N[a] - males$d15N[b]),
      abs(males$gradient[a] - males$gradient[b]))
  }, numeric(3))
  rowMeans(d, na.rm = TRUE)
})
obs_d <- c(mean(pr$abs_d13C), mean(pr$abs_d15N), mean(pr$abs_gradient))
pair_tab <- data.frame(measure = c("d13C", "d15N", "gradient score"), n_pairs = nrow(pr),
                       mean_abs_diff_same_male = obs_d, mean_abs_diff_year_matched = rowMeans(null_d),
                       P = (1 + rowSums(null_d <= obs_d)) / (N_PERM + 1))
pair_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
##          measure n_pairs mean_abs_diff_same_male mean_abs_diff_year_matched
## 1           d13C      10                   0.149                      1.160
## 2           d15N      10                   0.267                      0.618
## 3 gradient score      10                   0.373                      1.630
##        P
## 1 0.0001
## 2 0.0027
## 3 0.0001
write.csv(pair_tab, file.path(OUT, "5_within_male_differences.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

10 Suggested Methods text

Males were sampled for stable isotopes (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N) on arrival at the colony (2011–2013; n samples, n males) and measured for standard length; no tracking data were available. We tested for discrete isotopic groups with Gaussian mixture models allowing correlated isotopes (1–4 components; mclust), a parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of one vs two components, and by comparing the silhouette width of Ward clusters with that obtained from data simulated from a single bivariate normal distribution. Because these tests did not support discrete groups [update from results], we summarised isotopic variation as each male’s score on the first principal component of the standardised isotopes, and tested whether it varied with standard length, trip type and year (Freedman–Lane permutation tests, one sample per male). Male isotopic niche size (SEAc, SEA_B) and directional overlap with each female strategy were estimated with SIBER and nicheROVER (default non-informative prior), including a sensitivity analysis restricted to females sampled in the same years. Repeatability of isotope values was estimated with linear mixed models (trip type and year as fixed effects, individual as random effect; rptR), and within-male differences were compared with those between males sampled in the same years and trip types (9,999 randomisations).
